clue.text: City church to house master's old image of Christ

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London
CE is the Church of England
M is an abbreviation for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: A City of London church is to acquire an old painting of Christ by a master.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecce Homo, Latin for 'behold the man', is the name for paintings of Christ crowned with thorns, from Pilate's words.

clue.text: Film type of girl essentially turned on at the start

indicators.note: at the start places the turned word in front of the other piece
turned means the little word on is flipped round to read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned

indicators.note: essentially points to the core of the word girl, its middle letters

explanation.surface: A girl's taste in films seems to be what turns her on.
explanation.definitionFit: Film noir is a genre of dark, cynical crime movies, so noir names a type of film.

clue.text: Right to divide dodgy gear — stocking up with one?

indicators.note: to divide says the abbreviation for right splits the shuffled letters in two
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, signalling the letters of gear are rearranged

parts.note: Rt is the abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon

explanation.surface: Someone eyeing dodgy goods stocks up, perhaps from the back of a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To divide' puts RT between the halves of GAER, the anagram of gear signalled by 'dodgy'; the definition is a cryptic hint at what holds a stocking up.
explanation.definitionFit: A garter is a band that holds a stocking up, so with one in place the stocking stays up.

clue.text: Most agitated keeper conclusively struggles in goal

indicators.note: in says the following pieces go inside the word for goal

parts.note: a goal in football is the net

indicators.note: conclusively points to the very end of the word keeper

parts.note: vies means competes or struggles

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper flaps about in the goalmouth, looking the most rattled player on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerviest is the superlative of nervy, meaning jumpy or on edge, which matches most agitated.

clue.text: Sport sacking with tie lost

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have gone astray and must be put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A manager is sacked after a cup tie is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice skating is a winter sport of gliding on blades over ice, including figure and speed skating.

clue.text: Dive over nothing and waste time

indicators.note: over says the word for dive goes over, that is around, the zero

parts.note: a lunge is a sudden dive or thrust forward
O is a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A footballer dives over nothing at all and wastes time, as players do.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to laze about idly, frittering hours away doing nothing useful.

clue.text: Praise a storage medium with energy drink inside

indicators.note: inside says the drink sits within the abbreviation for the storage medium

parts.note: a CD, compact disc, is a storage medium
cola is a fizzy drink
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: An advert praises a disc that comes with an energy drink tucked inside the case.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or expression of high praise or honour.

clue.text: Sweet European girl

parts.note: Clair is a girl's name

explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a cream-filled choux pastry, a sweet treat or dessert.

clue.text: With following surprising score it's out of our hands

indicators.note: following means the abbreviation comes after the shuffled letters
surprising suggests an unexpected rearrangement of the word score

explanation.surface: After a surprising score, the result is beyond the team's control.
explanation.definitionFit: Money in escrow is held by a third party until conditions are met, so neither side controls it.

clue.text: Ultimately, England home before their postcards: relatives hide

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the next five words

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Fans in England send postcards home before their team plays, and relatives hide them.
explanation.definitionFit: Deerskin is the leather or hide made from a deer, so it is a type of hide.

clue.text: Lost Stevie G in poor showing

indicators.note: poor suggests a bad version of these letters, rearranged

parts.note: L stands for lost, as in a league table's won, drawn, lost columns
taken as written

explanation.surface: England lost with Stevie G, Steven Gerrard the England captain, having a poor showing.
explanation.definitionFit: Televising a match is broadcasting it, that is showing it on TV.

clue.text: It's used to pull women in closed boozer

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for women goes between the other pieces

parts.note: a door that is shut is to, as in 'pull the door to'
a boozer is a pub, a bar

explanation.surface: Someone goes to a lock-in at the pub hoping to pull women.
explanation.definitionFit: A towbar is the fitting on a car's rear for hitching and pulling a trailer or caravan.

clue.text: Worth going down in this exchange? Take score and extra time

definitions.text: Worth going down in this exchange?

parts.note: to bear is to take or endure
a mark is a score, as in an exam
ET is the abbreviation for extra time in football results

explanation.surface: A tense knockout match: the score is level and the game goes to extra time.
explanation.definitionFit: In a bear market on a stock exchange, share prices fall, so the worth of holdings is going down.

clue.text: Repeats Italian scores around English

indicators.note: around says the first two pieces together wrap the abbreviation for English

parts.note: rates means scores or grades

explanation.surface: An Italian side keeps scoring around the English defence, again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do or say something again, so iterates means repeats.

clue.text: Playing with Pirlo as star

indicators.note: playing with suggests toying with the letters to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Playing alongside Pirlo, Andrea Pirlo the Italian midfielder, as the star of the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the Pole Star, is the bright star nearest the north celestial pole.

clue.text: Main part for viewer, hard to watch for audience

parts.note: the iris is part of the eye, the body's viewer
H is short for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: for audience says the word for watch is heard rather than read

parts.note: to see is to watch

explanation.surface: Main part of a viewer's experience: hard to watch for the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old word for the open sea, so 'Main' is the definition, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic word for the sea, and the Irish Sea lies between Britain and Ireland.

clue.text: Rather late to drop wingers — one can shoot

indicators.note: dropping the wingers takes off the outer letters of the word late

parts.note: a rifle is a gun, something one can shoot

explanation.surface: Late in the game the manager drops his wingers so a striker can shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle used adverbially means slightly or somewhat, the same sense as rather.

clue.text: Left first class, back to England, home to get attacked

parts.note: A1 means first class, written AI

indicators.note: back to points to the last letter of the word England

parts.note: in means at home
taken as written

explanation.surface: A first-class player left and went back to England, home to be attacked by the press.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone is to attack them physically or verbally; laid into is its past tense.

clue.text: To him, even missing finals is appropriate

indicators.note: missing finals means each of the three words loses its last letter

explanation.surface: To him, even missing the finals is fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective after 'is', but it is a verb meaning steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate something is to take it for oneself without permission, which is stealing.

clue.text: Like mischievous conduct? Close to Manaus, training site is hot

indicators.note: close to points to the final letter of the word Manaus

parts.note: a camp is where a squad trains

explanation.definitionFit: Scampish behaviour is that of a scamp, a rascal, so it describes mischievous conduct.

clue.text: Relax, Italy, it's hot

parts.note: to chill is to relax
I is the international vehicle registration letter for Italy

explanation.surface: Telling Italy to calm down because it is hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilli is a fiery pepper, something spicy or hot to eat.

clue.text: Get good 10? Italian legend

parts.note: to bag is to get or obtain
10 written as letters looks like IO

explanation.surface: Getting a good number 10, the playmaker's shirt, means a great Italian player.
explanation.definitionFit: Roberto Baggio, Italy's famous number 10, is one of the country's greatest footballers.

clue.text: Post covered by Balotelli, ball's hoisted

indicators.note: hoisted says the hidden letters are read backwards
covered by says the answer lies concealed within the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A goalpost covered by Mario Balotelli, the Italian striker, as the ball is lifted high.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Post covered' as the definition, but 'covered by' signals the concealment, so the definition is just 'Post'. 'Hoisted', in a down clue, turns the letters upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet is a posting or job, and also lodging where soldiers are posted.

clue.text: Concerned with the runs in one area, old Roy Hodgson initially worried

indicators.note: worried suggests the letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of Roy and Hodgson

explanation.surface: Roy Hodgson, then England manager, is worried about the runs his team's opponents make.

clue.text: See 10
Soaks up sweat

parts.note: wets means soaks

explanation.surface: Something that soaks up sweat, like a towel.
explanation.definitionFit: To stew is to fret anxiously, and to sweat over something is the same idiom.

clue.text: Do take off — Cole's gutted

parts.note: to flee is to take off, run away

indicators.note: gutted means the insides of the name are removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Ashley Cole, the England defender, is gutted and takes off.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for cheating them, and fleecing is swindling them of money.

clue.text: They get hot in sun chasing lead?

indicators.note: chasing means the abbreviation for sun comes after

parts.note: lead is an example of a chemical element, hence the question mark
S is short for Sunday, here sun

explanation.surface: Things that get hot in the sun while chasing the lead in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Heating elements in kettles and ovens are the parts that become hot when current flows.
